answer: Agents hired to price marble, inspect a ledge, or map a reef must each lock 100 tokens for 30 days before bidding, and each bond permits only one active bid or job. Escrow prevents the same tokens from backing multiple identities at once. An attacker can still invent names, but operating 1,000 bidding identities requires locking 100,000 tokens, tying up capital and sacrificing its use elsewhere rather than gaining free influence.
